variants.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit / spacecraft concept development.
We are returning to L66. Image 1 is the ONLY design base. The owner liked specifically the LARGE UPPER-RIGHT REAR 3/4 of L66 and wants development of THAT EXACT functional construction.
DO NOT reinvent the ship or replace its tail with an ordinary aircraft fin, little triangle, plaque, tombstone, badge, antenna or ornamental plate. DO NOT make a massive stepped pedestal/building. Neither extreme is acceptable.

PRIMARY DESIGN TO PRESERVE FROM L66 REAR 3/4:
The broad original Liberty hull, two compact separated aft engines, central stern structure that rises smoothly between them into a substantial narrow TWO-SECTION MECHANICAL TAIL. Preserve the long sloping transition into the LOWER section, overlapping UPPER section, their real thickness, exposed stepping/overlap, and normal-sized equipment mounting plates on the sides. It is an integrated extension of the stern, with exactly the same overall height and visual mass as L66's rear-view tail (variation limited to about +/-10%). NOT a flat decorated fin sitting on the deck. Keep the tail centerline relatively narrow transversely, as L66, without a wide plinth or terrace. Keep the useful equipment surfaces and mechanical identity of the tail.
The UPPER-RIGHT REAR view in L66 has the cockpit toward RIGHT and the upper tail extending RIGHT toward that cockpit. This is the authoritative orientation. Copy this shape and direction into every view. In a front/side view with nose LEFT the same upper tail must therefore lean LEFT. Ignore the contradictory aft-raked upper-left front view of L66; the rear geometry wins.
The closed flat roof and visible cargo hatch remain ahead of the tail. Tail root stays at stern between engines. Engines remain accessible; equipment goes on tail, not engine covers.

LOCKED NATIVE PARTS:
Image 2 is authoritative for exactly THREE ordinary Defender fan blades per side: blue FRONT, green MIDDLE, amber REAR. Keep each full plate and free tip, recolored native pirate red; the middle blade cannot disappear. Common root at the lower FRONT edge of MAIN HULL after the short neck behind collar, not on the collar. Do not redesign wings or move roots. Fold three plates back/inward along flank in stowed view.
Image 3 is immutable source cabin and collar. Same capsule glass, frames, proportions, three separated collar ribs and original neck. Do not enlarge the canopy or add a brow.
Ignore image 2's old spoiler and vertical engine arrangement; the revised BODY/TWIN ENGINES come from L66 rear.

STYLE:
Keep L66's functional Freelancer Liberty pirate material treatment and original side Art Deco/Empire relief. Decorative style belongs to framed hull fields, rhythmic angled edges and restrained structural ribs. Do NOT add a little sunburst plaque on top as a substitute for a mechanical tail. No extra ornate carving, gold statues, palace elements, heavy rust, skeletal struts, piping or tiny rivets. Tail should use the same practical armor surfaces and mounting pads as L66.

PRESENTATION:
One neutral grey sheet. The MAIN large image occupying the LEFT 55% is REAR 3/4, matching L66's original rear camera (cockpit far RIGHT, exhausts near LEFT). It must clearly show the entire substantial two-section tail and its integrated stern root. A smaller FRONT 3/4 on upper RIGHT shows the same construction, not an alternative. Along bottom: SIDE FLIGHT nose LEFT, TOP, and SIDE STOWED nose LEFT. All are the SAME ship. Three wing blades remain visible; tail sections nest only modestly when stowed, not vanish. Match tail height, forward direction and stern attachment in all views. Labels only ID and view names.
VARIANT CONDITION:
L88. Faithful control: reproduce the L66 REAR 3/4 tail construction as closely as possible, keeping its lower sloping support, two nested angular sections and equipment flats. Only restore native three-leaf wings and fix forward orientation in the other views. No additional artistic redesign in this control variant. Label L88.
